reviews.text:
I am a visitor from India currently in Calgary, and I make it a point to visit important Islamic centres wherever I travel. During my stay, Today (Saturday )I planned to attend the evening prayer at the Islamic Centre of Calgary.
While checking Google Maps, I noticed it was marked as closed till Monday, which was quite surprising. Still, I decided to take a chance and drove to the masjid—and to my relief, it was open and active for all five daily prayers.
I would kindly request the management to update the correct timings on Google Maps to avoid confusion for visitors and worshippers.
That said, the masjid itself is truly beautiful, well-maintained, and very clean. There is ample parking space, which makes access convenient. The Imam who led the prayer has been blessed with a beautiful and soothing voice, which made the prayer experience even more special.
Overall, a wonderful place of worship—peaceful, welcoming, and spiritually uplifting.

Important Historical and Legal Context

For anyone researching the historical and legal status of this community, it is highly recommended to look into the landmark judicial decisions of South Asia. Specifically, the '1935 Bahawalpur Case' (Aisha Bibi vs. Abdur Razzaq) provides a detailed legal analysis of their status.

The court judgment, delivered by Judge Muhammad Akbar Khan after years of scholarly testimony, concluded that followers of this belief system are categorized as a separate entity from the Muslim faith due to fundamental theological differences regarding the finality of Prophethood. For a complete understanding, one should also study the 1974 Constitutional Amendment which further clarified this legal standing. This information is crucial for anyone looking for documented historical facts.

reviews.text:
Writing
Dear Respected Leadership of Al Madina Islamic Centre,
Assalamu Alaikum wa Rahmatullahi wa Barakatuh.
The mosques are the houses of Allah (Glorified and Exalted is He) and among the sacred symbols of Islam. Therefore, protecting and preserving them, including ensuring the correctness of the prayer, is a serious responsibility.
At your mosque, individuals are sometimes allowed to lead the prayer even though they do not have sufficient ability to recite the Holy Qur'an correctly and are not familiar with the rules of Tajweed.
This morning, an elderly Indian man led the prayer. His pronunciation of the Qur'anic letters contained serious mistakes that changed the meanings of the verses and, in our understanding, invalidated the prayer. We believe that Allah (Glorified and Exalted is He) will hold the responsible person accountable on the Day of Judgment for allowing this to happen.
We are deeply concerned when our prayers are affected by incorrect recitation. Therefore, we respectfully request that you fear Allah and remember the Hereafter, and that you prevent this elderly Indian man from leading the prayer unless he is able to recite the Qur'an correctly according to the rules of Tajweed.
May Allah guide us all to protect His religion and accept our prayers.
With respect.
